tier_reason: Intel's own arXiv paper (no venue stated) reports 2.4x/6.2x over TVM, 1.12x BERT-Large and 1.15x DLRM over oneDNN post-op fusion, FP32 4% worse / Int8 6% better than primitives on a Xeon Platinum 8358; no compiler, flags or benchmark code given, so first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: BERT Large 1.12x and DLRM 1.15x over oneDNN post-op fusion; MHA total time 2.3x (FP32) and 2.4x (Int8) lower than post-op fusion; 2.4x (MLP) and 6.2x (MHA) average over TVM, 3.8x on Int8 matmul total time; MLP total time 4% worse than primitives on FP32, 6% better on Int8

notes: Paper says the graph compiler is open source and embedded in oneDNN (cites github.com/oneapi-src/oneDNN) but names no subdirectory; repo_url left null and has_code unchanged since I did not open the oneDNN tree. Vendor (Intel) paper, so first-party.

tier_reason: Single-author arXiv paper (no venue found) by the repo author reports 2.5x single-thread / 1.7x multi-thread geomean over LIBXSMM SpMM, ~4x over dense BLAS at 95% sparsity and up to 5x over OpenVINO; autotune scripts exist in the repo but compiler/flags not stated, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 2.5x geomean over LIBXSMM SpMM single-threaded on Intel (1.7x multi-threaded); ~4x over dense BLAS at 95% sparsity (break-even ~70%); sparse conv 3.0x at 90% and 4.8x at 95% sparsity vs dense oneDNN on Intel; up to 5x throughput vs OpenVINO dense inference on pruneBERT

notes: Repo: Apache-2.0, 56 stars, 30 commits, not archived, last commit 2022-09-28 (abandoned) all confirmed. Paper does compare sparse conv against dense oneDNN, so the caveat 'oneDNN not directly compared' is slightly off; the AMD 1.3x / 22%-slower-than-SkimCaffe figures were not re-checked.

tier_reason: Upgraded C->B: the paper was published at ICLR 2025 (peer-reviewed proceedings page opened) and shows matching cuBLAS/FA3 on forward, 10-40% faster attention backward on H100 with CUDA 12.6; kernel code public but no nvcc flags stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: matches cuBLAS and FlashAttention-3 on GEMM and attention inference; 10-40% faster than FA3 on attention backward; 14x over FLA polynomial linear attention (6.5x learned-map); 7.9x (seq 1024) / 4.7x (seq 4096) over FlashFFTConv; README: ~855 TFLOPs H100 GEMM (~86% of peak)
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed (ICLR 2025) but authored by the project team; nvcc flags not stated. Matches rather than beats cuBLAS/FA3 on forward; wins are on backward and non-standard baselines (FLA, FlashFFTConv). No cuDNN attention comparison found in the paper. Current repo needs CUDA 12.8+, targets Hopper/Blackwell; Ampere no longer actively supported.

notes: Repo MIT, 3.7k stars, last commit 2026-09-12 (active), Together AI/Jump Trading/Cursor named in README; all confirmed. Baseline field mentions cuDNN attention, which the paper does not appear to test.
